qns_content.text: Which amine shows no reaction with \( \ce{HNO2} \) at 273-278 K?

text_solutions: Tertiary amines like \( \ce{(CH3CH2CH2)3N} \) do not react with \( \ce{HNO2} \) to form alcohols or nitrosamines, as per the PDF’s chemical properties.

qns_content.text: Which preparation method uses \( \ce{KOH} \) and \( \ce{Br2} \) to convert an amide to an amine?

text_solutions: The Hoffmann bromamide reaction uses \( \ce{Br2} \) and \( \ce{KOH} \) to convert an amide to an amine with one less carbon, as per the PDF’s preparation methods.

qns_content.text: The carbon chain length of the amine from \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CONH2} \) via Hoffmann bromamide reaction is:

text_solutions: Butanamide (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CONH2} \), 4 carbons) loses one carbon in the Hoffmann reaction, yielding propan-1-amine (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2NH2} \), 3 carbons), as per the PDF.

qns_content.text: The IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3CH2N(CH3)CH2CH3} \) is:

text_solutions: For tertiary amines, the largest alkyl group is the parent. Here, it’s ethanamine with N-methyl and N-ethyl groups, named N-ethyl-N-methylethanamine, as per the PDF.

qns_content.text: Which amine forms a yellow oily liquid with \( \ce{HNO2} \)?

text_solutions: Secondary amines like \( \ce{CH3CH2NHCH3} \) form nitrosamines (yellow oily liquids) with \( \ce{HNO2} \), as per the PDF’s chemical properties.

qns_content.text: The product of aniline reacting with excess \( \ce{Br2} \) in water is:

text_solutions: Aniline (\( \ce{C6H5NH2} \)) with excess \( \ce{Br2} \) in water forms 2,4,6-tribromoaniline due to the strong activation by \( \ce{-NH2} \), as per the PDF.

qns_content.text: The product of \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2NO2} \) reduction with \( \ce{Sn/HCl} \) is:

text_solutions: Reduction of 1-nitropropane (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2NO2} \)) with \( \ce{Sn/HCl} \) yields propan-1-amine (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2NH2} \)), as per the PDF’s preparation methods.

qns_content.text: Which amine has the lowest basicity in aqueous solution?

text_solutions: Aniline (\( \ce{C6H5NH2} \)) has the lowest basicity due to resonance delocalizing the nitrogen lone pair, as per the PDF’s basicity section.

qns_content.text: The IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2NHCH3} \) is:

text_solutions: The largest alkyl group is propyl, with an N-methyl substituent, named N-methylpropan-1-amine, as per the PDF’s nomenclature.

qns_content.text: Which amine has the highest solubility in water per carbon atom?

text_solutions: Methylamine (\( \ce{CH3NH2} \), 1C) has two N-H bonds for hydrogen bonding relative to one carbon, giving the highest solubility per carbon, as per the PDF.

qns_content.text: Which reagent acetylates the amino group of aniline?

text_solutions: Acetic anhydride (\( \ce{(CH3CO)2O} \)) reacts with aniline to form acetanilide by acetylating the \( \ce{-NH2} \) group, as described in the PDF’s chemical properties.

qns_content.text: The solubility of amines in water decreases with:

text_solutions: As per the PDF, solubility decreases with increasing alkyl chain length due to the growing hydrophobic nature, reducing hydrogen bonding with water.

qns_content.text: Which reaction produces a foul-smelling isocyanide from \( \ce{CH3NH2} \)?

text_solutions: The carbylamine reaction (\( \ce{CHCl3} \) + alcoholic KOH) with methylamine (\( \ce{CH3NH2} \)) forms methyl isocyanide (\( \ce{CH3NC} \)), as per the PDF.

qns_content.text: The reaction of \( \ce{CH3CH2NH2} \) with excess \( \ce{CH3Cl} \) yields:

text_solutions: Ethylamine (\( \ce{CH3CH2NH2} \)) with excess \( \ce{CH3Cl} \) forms N,N-dimethylethylamine (\( \ce{CH3CH2N(CH3)2} \)), a tertiary amine, as per the PDF’s alkylation.

qns_content.text: How many carbon atoms are in the product of \( \ce{CH3CH2NH2} \) with \( \ce{CH3COCl} \)?

text_solutions: Ethylamine (\( \ce{CH3CH2NH2} \), 2C) reacts with acetyl chloride (\( \ce{CH3COCl} \), 2C) to form N-ethylacetamide (\( \ce{CH3CONHCH2CH3} \), 4C), as per the PDF.

qns_content.text: The reaction of \( \ce{CH3CH2Cl} \) with excess \( \ce{NH3} \) primarily yields:

text_solutions: Ammonolysis of \( \ce{CH3CH2Cl} \) with excess \( \ce{NH3} \) favors the formation of the primary amine \( \ce{CH3CH2NH2} \) (ethylamine), as per the PDF’s preparation methods.

qns_content.text: A compound \( X \) on reduction with \( \ce{H2/Ni} \) gives \( \ce{CH3CH2NH2} \). \( X \) is:

text_solutions: Nitroethane (\( \ce{CH3CH2NO2} \)) is reduced to ethylamine (\( \ce{CH3CH2NH2} \)) with \( \ce{H2/Ni} \), as per the PDF’s preparation methods.

qns_content.text: The product of \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CONH2} \) undergoing Hoffmann bromamide reaction is:

text_solutions: Butanamide (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CONH2} \)) is converted to propan-1-amine (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2NH2} \)) by losing one carbon in the Hoffmann reaction, as per the PDF.

qns_content.text: Which amine has the least number of carbon atoms in its alkyl group?

text_solutions: Methylamine (\( \ce{CH3NH2} \)) has one carbon in its alkyl group, the least among the options, as per the PDF’s classification.

qns_content.text: Which amine forms a product with a benzene ring when reacted with \( \ce{H2SO4} \) at 453-473 K?

text_solutions: Aniline (\( \ce{C6H5NH2} \)) forms sulphanilic acid (\( \ce{H2NC6H4SO3H} \)) with a benzene ring when reacted with \( \ce{H2SO4} \) at high temperature, as per the PDF.

qns_content.text: The IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3CH(NH2)CH3} \) is:

text_solutions: The compound has a three-carbon chain with an amino group on the second carbon. In IUPAC, it’s named propan-2-amine.

qns_content.text: Which method uses phthalimide to prepare primary amines?

text_solutions: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis uses phthalimide with an alkyl halide to selectively prepare primary amines, as detailed in the PDF.

qns_content.text: Which of the following amines does not liberate \( \ce{N2} \) gas with \( \ce{HNO2} \)?

text_solutions: Tertiary amines like \( \ce{(CH3CH2)3N} \) do not react with \( \ce{HNO2} \) to liberate \( \ce{N2} \), unlike primary aliphatic amines, as per the PDF.

qns_content.text: The hybridization of nitrogen in the product of \( \ce{CH3NH2} \) with \( \ce{CH3COCl} \) is:

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH3NH2} \) forms \( \ce{CH3NHCOCH3} \) with \( \ce{CH3COCl} \). Nitrogen has three sigma bonds and one lone pair, remaining \( sp^3 \), as per the PDF’s structure.

qns_content.text: Which of the following has the least number of hydrogen atoms attached to nitrogen?

text_solutions: Tertiary amines like \( \ce{(CH3)3N} \) have no hydrogen atoms on nitrogen, unlike primary (2 H) and secondary (1 H) amines, as per the PDF.

qns_content.text: The boiling point of \( \ce{(CH3)2NH} \) is lower than \( \ce{CH3CH2NH2} \) due to:

text_solutions: \( \ce{(CH3)2NH} \) (secondary) has one N-H bond, while \( \ce{CH3CH2NH2} \) (primary) has two, leading to less hydrogen bonding and a lower boiling point, as per the PDF.

qns_content.text: How many hydrogen atoms are directly attached to nitrogen in \( \ce{(CH3CH2)2NH} \)?

text_solutions: Diethylamine (\( \ce{(CH3CH2)2NH} \)), a secondary amine, has one hydrogen atom directly attached to nitrogen, as per the PDF’s structure.

qns_content.text: What is the major product when aniline reacts with excess bromine water?

text_solutions: Aniline (\( \ce{C6H5NH2} \)) undergoes electrophilic substitution with excess bromine water, forming 2,4,6-tribromoaniline due to the strong activating effect of the \( \ce{-NH2} \) group.

qns_content.text: Which statement is true about the basicity of \( \ce{C6H5NH2} \) compared to \( \ce{CH3NH2} \)?

options.text: \( \ce{C6H5NH2} \) is more basic due to resonance
\( \ce{C6H5NH2} \) is more basic due to inductive effect
\( \ce{C6H5NH2} \) is less basic due to resonance
\( \ce{C6H5NH2} \) is less basic due to steric hindrance

text_solutions: Aniline (\( \ce{C6H5NH2} \)) is less basic than methylamine (\( \ce{CH3NH2} \)) due to resonance delocalizing the nitrogen lone pair, as per the PDF’s basicity section.

qns_content.text: Which method is preferred for preparing primary amines without forming secondary or tertiary amines?

text_solutions: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis selectively produces primary amines by reacting phthalimide with an alkyl halide, followed by hydrolysis, avoiding mixtures of secondary and tertiary amines seen in ammonolysis.

qns_content.text: Which amine turns bromine water colorless due to substitution?

text_solutions: Aniline (\( \ce{C6H5NH2} \)) undergoes electrophilic substitution with \( \ce{Br2} \) in water, forming 2,4,6-tribromoaniline and decolorizing bromine, as per the PDF.

qns_content.text: A primary amine \( X \) reacts with \( \ce{HNO2} \) to give \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2OH} \). \( X \) is:

text_solutions: Butan-1-amine (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2NH2} \)) reacts with \( \ce{HNO2} \) to form butan-1-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2OH} \)) and \( \ce{N2} \), as per the PDF.

qns_content.text: An amine \( X \) reacts with \( \ce{CH3CH2Cl} \) to form a tertiary amine. \( X \) could be:

text_solutions: A secondary amine like \( \ce{CH3NHCH3} \) reacts with \( \ce{CH3CH2Cl} \) to add an ethyl group, forming a tertiary amine (\( \ce{CH3CH2N(CH3)2} \)), as per the PDF’s alkylation.

qns_content.text: Which amine produces a yellow oily liquid on reaction with \( \ce{HNO2} \)?

text_solutions: Secondary amines like \( \ce{(CH3CH2)2NH} \) react with \( \ce{HNO2} \) to form yellow oily nitrosamines (e.g., \( \ce{(CH3CH2)2N-NO} \)), as described in the PDF’s chemical tests.

qns_content.text: The number of lone pairs on nitrogen in \( \ce{(CH3)3N} \) is:

text_solutions: In trimethylamine (\( \ce{(CH3)3N} \)), nitrogen has three sigma bonds to carbon and one lone pair, as per the PDF’s structure section.

qns_content.text: The number of lone pairs on nitrogen in \( \ce{CH3CH2NHCH3} \) is:

text_solutions: In \( \ce{CH3CH2NHCH3} \), nitrogen has three sigma bonds (two C, one H) and one lone pair, as per the PDF’s structure.

qns_content.text: The product of \( \ce{CH3CH2NH2} \) with \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2COCl} \) is:

text_solutions: Ethylamine (\( \ce{CH3CH2NH2} \)) reacts with butanoyl chloride (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2COCl} \)) to form N-ethylbutanamide (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CONHCH2CH3} \)), as per the PDF’s acylation.

qns_content.text: An amine \( X \) reacts with \( \ce{CHCl3} \) and KOH to form \( \ce{CH3CH2NC} \). \( X \) is:

text_solutions: Ethylamine (\( \ce{CH3CH2NH2} \)) forms ethyl isocyanide (\( \ce{CH3CH2NC} \)) in the carbylamine reaction, as per the PDF’s chemical properties.

qns_content.text: The basic strength of aniline is less than aliphatic amines due to:

text_solutions: Resonance in aniline delocalizes the nitrogen lone pair into the benzene ring, reducing basicity compared to aliphatic amines, as per the PDF.

qns_content.text: Which amine does not react with benzenesulphonyl chloride?

text_solutions: Tertiary amines like \( \ce{(CH3CH2)3N} \) lack a hydrogen on nitrogen to form sulphonamides with benzenesulphonyl chloride, unlike primary and secondary amines.

qns_content.text: Which amine requires the least number of steps to prepare from \( \ce{CH3Cl} \) using \( \ce{NH3} \)?

text_solutions: Methylamine (\( \ce{CH3NH2} \)) is formed directly from \( \ce{CH3Cl} \) and \( \ce{NH3} \) in one step via ammonolysis, as per the PDF’s preparation methods.

qns_content.text: The compound formed when ethylamine reacts with chloroform and alcoholic KOH is:

text_solutions: Ethylamine (\( \ce{CH3CH2NH2} \)) undergoes the carbylamine reaction with \( \ce{CHCl3} \) and alcoholic KOH to form ethyl isocyanide (\( \ce{CH3CH2NC} \)), as per the PDF.

qns_content.text: The hybridization of nitrogen in \( \ce{(CH3CH2)3N} \) is:

text_solutions: In triethylamine (\( \ce{(CH3CH2)3N} \)), nitrogen has three sigma bonds to carbon and one lone pair, indicating \( sp^3 \) hybridization, as per the PDF’s structure.

qns_content.text: The weakest base in aqueous solution among the following is:

text_solutions: Aniline (\( \ce{C6H5NH2} \)) is the weakest due to resonance delocalizing the nitrogen lone pair, as per the PDF’s basicity discussion.

qns_content.text: The strongest base in gaseous phase among the following is:

text_solutions: Trimethylamine (\( \ce{(CH3)3N} \)) has three electron-donating methyl groups, making it the strongest base in the gaseous phase, as per the PDF.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is not a physical property of amines?

options.text: High boiling point due to hydrogen bonding

text_solutions: Reaction with \( \ce{HNO2} \) is a chemical property, not a physical one like boiling point or solubility, as per the PDF’s physical properties section.

qns_content.text: Which amine gives a foul-smelling compound on reaction with \( \ce{CHCl3} \) and alcoholic KOH?

text_solutions: Primary amines like \( \ce{CH3NH2} \) react with \( \ce{CHCl3} \) and alcoholic KOH to form isocyanides (e.g., \( \ce{CH3NC} \)), which have a foul odor, as per the PDF’s carbylamine test.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a primary aliphatic amine?

text_solutions: Ethylamine (\( \ce{CH3CH2NH2} \)) has one alkyl group attached to nitrogen and no aryl group, making it a primary aliphatic amine, as per the PDF’s classification.

qns_content.text: Which compound is formed when benzyl chloride undergoes ammonolysis followed by reaction with two moles of \( \ce{CH3Cl} \)?

text_solutions: Benzyl chloride (\( \ce{C6H5CH2Cl} \)) with \( \ce{NH3} \) forms benzylamine (\( \ce{C6H5CH2NH2} \)), which reacts with two \( \ce{CH3Cl} \) to form \( \ce{C6H5CH2N(CH3)2} \) (N,N-dimethylbenzylamine).

qns_content.text: Which property of aniline allows it to undergo electrophilic substitution at ortho and para positions?

text_solutions: The \( \ce{-NH2} \) group in aniline is electron-donating due to resonance, activating the ring and directing substitution to ortho and para positions, as per the PDF.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is an aromatic amine?

text_solutions: Aniline (\( \ce{C6H5NH2} \)) has the \( \ce{-NH2} \) group directly attached to a benzene ring, classifying it as an aromatic amine, as per the PDF.

qns_content.text: Which of the following amines is most soluble in water?

text_solutions: Solubility decreases with increasing alkyl chain length due to reduced hydrogen bonding. \( \ce{CH3NH2} \) (smallest chain) is most soluble, as per the PDF’s physical properties.

qns_content.text: Which reaction of \( \ce{CH3NH2} \) produces a compound with a characteristic foul odor?

text_solutions: The carbylamine reaction of \( \ce{CH3NH2} \) with \( \ce{CHCl3} \) and KOH forms methyl isocyanide (\( \ce{CH3NC} \)), known for its foul odor, as per the PDF.

qns_content.text: Which physical property decreases as the amine order increases from primary to tertiary?

text_solutions: Hydrogen bonding decreases from primary (two N-H) to secondary (one N-H) to tertiary (no N-H), as per the PDF’s physical properties.

qns_content.text: An amide \( X \) on Hoffmann bromamide reaction gives \( \ce{CH3CH2NH2} \). \( X \) is:

text_solutions: Propanamide (\( \ce{CH3CH2CONH2} \)) loses one carbon in the Hoffmann reaction to form ethylamine (\( \ce{CH3CH2NH2} \)), as per the PDF.

qns_content.text: The product of \( \ce{CH3CH2NH2} \) reacting with excess \( \ce{CH3Cl} \) is:

text_solutions: Ethylamine (\( \ce{CH3CH2NH2} \)) with excess \( \ce{CH3Cl} \) undergoes alkylation to form \( \ce{CH3CH2N(CH3)2} \) (N,N-dimethylethylamine), a tertiary amine, as per the PDF.

qns_content.text: Which method selectively produces primary amines without secondary or tertiary byproducts?

text_solutions: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis produces only primary amines by reacting phthalimide with an alkyl halide, as per the PDF’s preparation methods.

qns_content.text: An alkyl halide \( X \) reacts with \( \ce{NH3} \) to give \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2NH2} \). \( X \) is:

text_solutions: 1-Chloropropane (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2Cl} \)) undergoes ammonolysis with \( \ce{NH3} \) to form propan-1-amine (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2NH2} \)), as per the PDF’s preparation methods.

qns_content.text: The product of \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2NH2} \) with \( \ce{CH3CH2Cl} \) in the presence of a base is:

text_solutions: Propan-1-amine (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2NH2} \)) reacts with \( \ce{CH3CH2Cl} \) and a base to form N-ethylpropan-1-amine (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2NHCH2CH3} \)), as per the PDF’s alkylation.

qns_content.text: The product of \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2NO2} \) reduction with \( \ce{H2/Ni} \) is:

text_solutions: Reduction of 1-nitrobutane (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2NO2} \)) with \( \ce{H2/Ni} \) yields butan-1-amine (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2NH2} \)), as per the PDF’s preparation methods.

qns_content.text: The product of \( \ce{C6H5NH2} \) reacting with one mole of \( \ce{CH3COCl} \) is:

text_solutions: Aniline (\( \ce{C6H5NH2} \)) reacts with one mole of acetyl chloride to form acetanilide (\( \ce{C6H5NHCOCH3} \)), as per the PDF’s acetylation reaction.

qns_content.text: Which test produces a foul odor with primary aliphatic amines?

text_solutions: The carbylamine test (\( \ce{CHCl3} \) + alcoholic KOH) with primary aliphatic amines forms isocyanides, which have a foul odor, as per the PDF’s chemical properties.

qns_content.text: Aniline on nitration gives a significant amount of:

text_solutions: In strong acidic medium, aniline protonates to form anilinium ion, which is meta-directing, leading to substantial m-nitroaniline alongside ortho and para isomers.

qns_content.text: The hybridization of nitrogen in \( \ce{CH3NH2} \) is:

text_solutions: In methylamine (\( \ce{CH3NH2} \)), nitrogen is bonded to one carbon and two hydrogens, with a lone pair, resulting in \( sp^3 \) hybridization, as noted in the PDF’s structure section.

qns_content.text: The IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3N(CH2CH3)2} \) is:

text_solutions: For tertiary amines, the largest alkyl group is the parent. Here, ethanamine with N-methyl and N-ethyl substituents is N-ethyl-N-methylethanamine, as per the PDF.

qns_content.text: Which amine can be prepared by reducing \( \ce{CH3CH2NO2} \) with \( \ce{H2/Ni} \)?

text_solutions: Reduction of nitroethane (\( \ce{CH3CH2NO2} \)) with \( \ce{H2/Ni} \) yields ethylamine (\( \ce{CH3CH2NH2} \)), as per the PDF’s preparation methods.

qns_content.text: Which amine forms a sulphonamide insoluble in alkali with \( \ce{C6H5SO2Cl} \)?

text_solutions: Secondary amines like \( \ce{(CH3CH2)2NH} \) form sulphonamides lacking an acidic hydrogen, insoluble in alkali, as per the PDF’s Hinsberg test.

qns_content.text: The product of \( \ce{CH3CH2NH2} \) reacting with \( \ce{HNO2} \) at 273-278 K is:

text_solutions: Ethylamine (\( \ce{CH3CH2NH2} \)) reacts with \( \ce{HNO2} \) to form ethanol (\( \ce{CH3CH2OH} \)) and \( \ce{N2} \), as per the PDF’s chemical properties.

qns_content.text: The product of the reaction \( \ce{CH3CH2NH2 + HCl ->} \) is:

text_solutions: Ethanamine, a basic amine, reacts with HCl to form its salt, ethylammonium chloride (\( \ce{CH3CH2NH3^+ Cl^-} \)).

qns_content.text: The boiling point trend for amines of similar molecular weight is:

text_solutions: For similar molecular weights, primary > secondary > tertiary due to decreasing hydrogen bonding, as per the PDF’s physical properties (e.g., \( \ce{CH3CH2NH2} \) > \( \ce{(CH3)2NH} \) > \( \ce{(CH3)3N} \)).

qns_content.text: Which amine forms a precipitate insoluble in NaOH with benzenesulphonyl chloride?

text_solutions: Secondary amines like \( \ce{CH3CH2NHCH3} \) form sulphonamides insoluble in alkali in the Hinsberg test, as per the PDF.

qns_content.text: The bond angle around nitrogen in \( \ce{(CH3CH2)2NH} \) is closest to:

text_solutions: Diethylamine (\( \ce{(CH3CH2)2NH} \)) has \( sp^3 \) hybridized nitrogen with a lone pair, giving a bond angle slightly less than 109.5° (around 107°-108°), as per the PDF’s structure.

qns_content.text: The amine produced from \( \ce{CH3CONH2} \) via Hoffmann bromamide reaction is:

text_solutions: Ethanamide (\( \ce{CH3CONH2} \)) loses one carbon in the Hoffmann reaction to form methylamine (\( \ce{CH3NH2} \)), as per the PDF.

qns_content.text: Which amine does not produce \( \ce{N2} \) gas with \( \ce{HNO2} \)?

text_solutions: Tertiary amines like \( \ce{(CH3CH2)3N} \) do not react with \( \ce{HNO2} \) to form \( \ce{N2} \), unlike primary aliphatic amines, as per the PDF.

qns_content.text: Which of the following does not form a salt with dilute HCl?

text_solutions: Tertiary amines like \( \ce{(CH3CH2)3N} \) form salts with HCl due to the lone pair on nitrogen. However, \( \ce{CH3CONH2} \) (an amide) is not basic enough to form a salt, as per the PDF.

qns_content.text: An amine \( X \) forms a precipitate with \( \ce{Br2} \) water but not with \( \ce{HNO2} \). \( X \) is:

text_solutions: Aniline (\( \ce{C6H5NH2} \)) forms 2,4,6-tribromoaniline with \( \ce{Br2} \) water (precipitate) but does not liberate \( \ce{N2} \) with \( \ce{HNO2} \) like aliphatic primary amines, as per the PDF.

qns_content.text: The product of \( \ce{C6H5NH2} \) with \( \ce{CH3CH2COCl} \) is:

text_solutions: Aniline (\( \ce{C6H5NH2} \)) reacts with propanoyl chloride (\( \ce{CH3CH2COCl} \)) to form N-phenylpropanamide (\( \ce{C6H5NHCOCH2CH3} \)), as per the PDF’s acylation.

qns_content.text: Which amine is produced from \( \ce{CH3CH2CONH2} \) via Hoffmann bromamide reaction?

text_solutions: Propanamide (\( \ce{CH3CH2CONH2} \)) loses one carbon in the Hoffmann reaction to form ethylamine (\( \ce{CH3CH2NH2} \)), as per the PDF.

qns_content.text: Which reagent is used to distinguish primary amines from secondary amines by forming a soluble product in alkali?

text_solutions: Benzenesulphonyl chloride (Hinsberg’s reagent) reacts with primary amines to form sulphonamides with an acidic hydrogen, soluble in alkali. Secondary amines form insoluble sulphonamides without acidic hydrogen.

qns_content.text: Which amine has the highest boiling point?

text_solutions: Primary amines like \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2NH2} \) have stronger hydrogen bonding than secondary or tertiary amines, leading to a higher boiling point, as per the PDF.

qns_content.text: The IUPAC name of \( \ce{(CH3)2NCH2CH3} \) is:

text_solutions: For tertiary amines, the largest alkyl group is the parent chain. Here, ethyl (\( \ce{CH2CH3} \)) is the parent, with two methyl groups on nitrogen, named N,N-dimethylethanamine, as per the PDF.

qns_content.text: The reaction of \( \ce{CH3NH2} \) with \( \ce{HNO2} \) produces:

text_solutions: Methylamine (\( \ce{CH3NH2} \)), a primary aliphatic amine, reacts with \( \ce{HNO2} \) to form methanol (\( \ce{CH3OH} \)) and \( \ce{N2} \), as per the PDF.

qns_content.text: Which compound is formed when \( \ce{CH3CH2CONH2} \) reacts with \( \ce{Br2} \) and \( \ce{KOH} \)?

text_solutions: Hoffmann bromamide reaction converts \( \ce{CH3CH2CONH2} \) (propanamide) to \( \ce{CH3CH2NH2} \) (ethylamine), reducing the carbon chain by one, as per the PDF.

qns_content.text: Which amine can be separated from a mixture using the Hinsberg test with alkali?

text_solutions: Primary amines like \( \ce{CH3CH2NH2} \) form sulphonamides soluble in alkali, allowing separation, as per the PDF’s Hinsberg test.

qns_content.text: The boiling point of \( \ce{CH3NH2} \) is higher than \( \ce{(CH3)3N} \) due to:

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH3NH2} \) (primary) forms hydrogen bonds, while \( \ce{(CH3)3N} \) (tertiary) does not, leading to a higher boiling point for the former, as per the PDF.

qns_content.text: Which amine cannot be prepared by Gabriel phthalimide synthesis?

text_solutions: Aromatic amines like \( \ce{C6H5NH2} \) cannot be prepared by Gabriel synthesis, which is limited to aliphatic primary amines, as per the PDF.

qns_content.text: The reaction of aniline with concentrated \( \ce{H2SO4} \) at 453-473 K produces:

text_solutions: Aniline forms anilinium hydrogensulphate, which rearranges on heating to p-aminobenzene sulphonic acid (sulphanilic acid).

qns_content.text: Which property explains the basic nature of amines?

text_solutions: Hoffmann bromamide reaction converts \( \ce{CH3CONH2} \) (ethanamide) to \( \ce{CH3NH2} \) (methylamine), reducing the carbon chain by one, as detailed in the PDF.

qns_content.text: An alkyl halide \( X \) with \( \ce{NH3} \) gives \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2NH2} \). \( X \) is:

text_solutions: 1-Chlorobutane (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2Cl} \)) reacts with \( \ce{NH3} \) via ammonolysis to form butan-1-amine (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2NH2} \)), as per the PDF.

qns_content.text: Why does aniline not undergo Friedel-Crafts reaction?

text_solutions: Aniline’s nitrogen forms a salt with \( \ce{AlCl3} \) (Lewis acid catalyst), acquiring a positive charge and deactivating the ring for electrophilic substitution.

qns_content.text: A compound \( X \) on reduction with \( \ce{H2/Ni} \) gives \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2NH2} \). \( X \) is:

text_solutions: Reduction of 1-nitropropane (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2NO2} \)) with \( \ce{H2/Ni} \) yields propan-1-amine (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2NH2} \)), as per the PDF’s preparation methods.

qns_content.text: The IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2NH2} \) is:

text_solutions: The compound has a four-carbon chain with an amine group on the first carbon, named butan-1-amine, as per the PDF’s nomenclature.

qns_content.text: The order of reactivity of amines with \( \ce{CH3COCl} \) is:

text_solutions: Reactivity decreases as substitution on nitrogen increases due to steric hindrance and lone pair availability: primary > secondary > tertiary, as per the PDF’s chemical properties.

qns_content.text: Which amine would form the smallest alcohol when reacted with \( \ce{HNO2} \)?

text_solutions: Methylamine (\( \ce{CH3NH2} \)) reacts with \( \ce{HNO2} \) to form methanol (\( \ce{CH3OH} \)), the smallest alcohol, as per the PDF’s chemical properties.

qns_content.text: Which of the following has the highest solubility in water?

text_solutions: Solubility depends on hydrogen bonding with water. \( \ce{CH3NH2} \) (primary amine) forms more hydrogen bonds than \( \ce{(CH3)2NH} \) (secondary) or \( \ce{(CH3)3N} \) (tertiary), and \( \ce{C6H5NH2} \) has lower solubility due to the hydrophobic benzene ring.
